newsitem.title: USA: Wide arbitrage pulls Brent crude into US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Wide arbitrage pulls Brent crude into US Gulf.

text.p: A wide transatlantic arbitrage fueled a wave of Brent crude offerings into the U.S. Gulf Coast on Thursday, putting pressure on regional sweet grades, traders said.
"Directionally Brent has changed a lot," said a Gulf Coast trader. "There's potential for a whole lot of cargoes to come over."
A U.S. company was heard to have sold a Brent cargo at a discount of around 80 cents to bennchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for delivery June 22-27.
Two trading houses were offering the North Sea crude into the Gulf Coast for delivery June 22-28 and June 25-July 2, asking around WTI/Cushing minus 70-80 cents a barrel, traders said.
Another offer was heard for June 22-28 at around 70 cents a barrel under WTI/Cushing.
Brent was offered at 50-55 cents under WTI/Cushing earlier this week, underscoring the abrupt softening in prices for sweet barrels in the Gulf.
The wave of Brents coming into the Gulf was attributed to the wide transatlantic arbitrage as well as weak refining margins and consequent run cuts in Europe, traders said.
The June Brent loading program did not turn out to be as light as some traders had anticipated as a result of maintenance.
The June Brent program scheduled the equivalent of 38.4 cargoes, including top-ups, down from the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes in May.
The June spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.80 a barrel Thursday afternoon, up some 25-30 cents from Wednesday afternoon.
Dated Brent was thinly talked around June Brent minus 25 cents a barrel in Europe, traders said.
The Gulf Coast was also attracting its share of West African barrels despite a pickup in Asian buying, traders said.
A European company was weighing bringing over a VLCC of Nigerian Bonny Light for June 20-25 arrival, asking dated Brent plus $1.65-70 a barrel into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).

Market talk of a possible delivery of Bonny Light into the NYMEX upon expiry of the June contract on May 20 persisted. Exchange for Physical (EFP) transactions were runniung around five to seven cents a barrel, traders said.

In Latin America, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol was heard to have sold a Cusiana cargo for June 26-30 loading at around $1.23 a barrel under WTI/Cushing fob, up two cents from the last confirmed deal.
Ecopetrol was offering another Cusiana cargo for loading June 14-18.
Amid the flood of foreign barrels, the Gulf Coast appetite for crude was seen as waning.
"I think a lot of people are full already (for June), and margins certainly aren't going our way," said a Gulf Coast refiner.
